Damage at Akutan reported by local emergency manager: Construction materials at a new fourplex blown away. Very strong winds still occurring.

A person riding a snow mobile in a remote area was caught in an avalanche and perished. The area was only accessible by helicopter or snow mobile.

The McHugh Creek Fire initiated along the Seward highway on July 16th. It smoldered for two or three days, but then dry northerly winds caused the fire to grow and threaten the highway. This fire was close to several Anchorage subdivisions and evacuations were considered but not required. No structures were destroyed but the firefighting agencies estimate $6M was spent on firefighting efforts.

Winds began the afternoon of 9/11 and continued overnight. Several power outages in Chugiak and Eagle River were reported. Roof damage, including from downed trees, was sustained in Palmer and Anchorage.
Glen Alps mesonet station reported 82 mph gusts. Up to 8000 people in the Anchorage area lost power. Damage to lawn furniture was reported.
Portage glacier AWOS reported 78 mph gust.
Cordova Boat Harbor reported a gust to 87 mph on 9/21. Cape Hinchinbrook entrance to Prince William Sound was closed to outbound laden tankers due to weather.
Eleven to 14 inches of snow was reported by trained spotters in the Trapper Creek to Petersville area.

About 3.5 inches of rain fell in the Seward area, with 1.72 inches falling in a 6 hour period. The Resurrection River, adjacent to the Seward airport, rose 5 ft in 24 hours, resulting in water and debris impacting the runway and causing a 2 day closure of the airport.
Winds reached 91 mph at Adak Naval Station.
Unalaska Airport measured a wind gust at 79 knots.
Buoy 46070 reported a gust to 74 kt followed by seas to 47.9 feet.

Several days of heavy rain caused the waters of Indian Creek in the City of Chignik to rise to bankfull for several days. This prolonged high-water condition led to scour along the abutments and resulted in compromise of the structural integrity of the municipal vehicle bridge as well as the pedestrian bridge in town.
King Cove ASOS recorded a gust of 66 knots at 5 p.m.

Blizzard conditions were created throughout Thompson Pass as winds to 111 mph picked up and drifted snow through the area. Less than 1/4 mile visibilities and white-out conditions were reported from DOT officials as early as 4 am on the 26th of Jan. These conditions persisted through approximately 7pm on the 26th. Strong winds continued to effect the area as late as 11pm but visibilities had improved to greater than 1 mile as early as 7pm.
Winds at King Cove were above 73 mph for over 6 hrs. No damage was observed.

Adak ASOS measured 62 knots of wind. Surface pressure chart indicates winds met criteria.
St George ASOS measured a peak wind at 72 knots.

Two snowmachiners triggered an avalanche near Snug Harbor, Alaska.  One person escaped and was able to locate the other person, who was already deceased. This was reported in the Alaska Dispatch News.
Estimated wind gusts in the Copper River Delta based on wind in Thompson Pass and Valdez characterizing the magnitude of the gap wind.

Dispatcher reported widespread damage across Cordova. Many trees have been blown over or snapped with several of them falling on houses. Anywhere from one to two dozen structures have sustained roof damage from falling or breaking trees. Several boats have been damaged. Much of the damage reported is along the Copper River highway from mile 6 to 6 and a half. An estimation of 30 to 40 uprooted trees. Estimated wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph from the northwest.

Dispatcher reported widespread minor wind damage across Valdez. Multiple light poles have been blown over or damaged...multiple buildings with siding removed and several other structures across town damaged or destroyed. Hurricane force wind gusts have been observed since 17z.

White-out conditions (with wind) were most definitely observed last night through this morning. Saint Paul reported 1/16th of a mile visibility in snow and blowing snow. Peak winds reached 49 knots. No reports of damage.

Police at Dutch Harbor had no reports of structural damage, however there were many vehicles stuck in the snow.  A travel advisory was issued to try to keep people off the roads.  Road crews worked late into Sunday night to clear the roads before the morning commute.  No Road impacts reported Monday.

Multiple Motorist reported White out conditions while in travel. The D.O.T. worker in the Pass also reported blizzard conditions in Thompson Pass and at Keystone Canyon.
Spotter report from King Cove of white out conditions and drifting.
Department of Highways workers reported wind speed of 30 to 40 mph and blowing snow that reduced the visibility to less than a quarter mile this morning at 6 A.M.

Department of Highways Road Weather Information Site at Mchugh Creek.

Flooding in many yards and at least one cabin along Snug Harbor Road. The lake edge is normally about another 30 feet off the deck. NWS survey crews found flooded boat launches at both Cooper Landing Boat Launch and Quartz Creek Campground Boat Launch. The public also reported flooding of various parking lots around the Cooper Landing area via Social Media.

NWS Survey team as well as photos and reports from residents along Primrose Spur road on south end of Kenai Lake confirm several days of flooded yards and road closed by state Dept. of Transportation. Resident reported flooding on the high end of normal for this biennial flooding event.

Refuge Manager from the Togiak Wildlife Refuge reported that the Kanektok River overflowed. The spit separating the river from the lagoon was under water. The archaeological site south of Quinhagak had a 3-4' retaining wall of tundra and sand bags that eroded away exposing more of the site. Water flooded the water plant road, about 1/2 mile from Quinhagak to the water intake. The boat harbor flooded.

Winds peaked shortly after 6 AM at 75 mph at the St. Paul Aiport. Minor erosion, roof damage and siding damage was documented by the local Weather Service Office. The ASOS at St. George Airport peaked at 61 kts around the same time.

False Pass AWOS reported a wind gust of 78 mph at 14:50 AKDT. Nelson Lagoon AWOS reported a wind gust of 82 mph at 18:35 AKDT. Multiple other observations across the Alaska Peninsula reported wind gusts between 65 and 74 mph including Cold Bay and King Cove. No reports of any structural damage.
Peak gust of 66 knots reported at Atka (PAAK) at 05:33 and by the next observation at 05:56 the winds had already begun to diminish.
Shemya (PASY) observed hurricane force wind gusts for nearly 3 hours before winds began to diminish. Winds stayed above 70 mph for another 2 hours following them diminishing below warning criteria.
PAIL (Iliamna Airport) reported 8 inches of snowfall.

Multiple reports of 9 to 12 of snowfall fell near and east of Skwentna. The base of Mount Susitna reported 7 inches of snow while Talkeetna reported 8.5 inches of snow. Storm Total Reports: 11 inches at Bentalit Lodge, 12 to 18 inches at the Cantwell DOT and 12.5 inches at the Chulitna DOT.
NWS Employee suffered structural damage to house due to high winds. Sections of fencing were blown down and minor to moderate roof damage was reported due to shingles being removed by high winds.
Mesonet site in Potter Marsh recorded a wind speed of 78 mph at 10:36 and a max wind gust of 87 mph at 11:30.
Multiple reports of winds in excess of 65 kts across the Anchorage Hillside. Chugach Electric Compacy reported over 3000 houses without power due to wind damage to the utilities.
Max wind gust of 85 mph late in the morning near Glen Alps. Some trees were down in the area and power was out.
Reports of wind gusts up to 80 mph and siding missing from a house near Glen Alps.

St George ASOS reported a gust of 78 knots. Damage was sustained at the KUHB radio station on St Paul when the radio tower blew over.
False Pass AWOS reported a gust to 66 kts at 9:12 a.m. Warning level winds were also observed at Cold Bay and King Cove.
Akutan AWOS measured 76 knot winds at 2:35 a.m. Warning level winds were also observed at Unalaska airport.
The Road Weather Information System site near Wortmann's Gorge reported a gust to 76 mph. A wind gust of 83 mph was also observed at Valdez airport.
Unalaska airport experienced a peak gust of 91 mph during this period. Minor damage was sustained: an airport gate broke, rocks were thrown onto the runway and a vessel broke free in the harbor.
The NOS NWLON at Adak recorded a peak wind gust of 91 mph.
The NOS NWLON at Nikolski reported winds gusting to 75 mph.
An avalanche in Hatcher Pass took the life of a local ski coach. Strong winds earlier in the week and low snow caused the snowpack to be very unstable.

Thompson Pass received 40 inches of snow in a 24 hour period. 15 inches of snowfall were measured in a 90 minute period, close to a record snowfall rate. The road through the pass was closed due to avalanche danger.
Eureka Lodge reported 14 inches of snowfall in 24 hours.
Mesonet stations on the Upper Hillside reported close to 80 mph wind gusts.

Anchorage Daily News reported wind damage in Quinhagak. 85 mph winds were cited but could not be confirmed. An unfinished house blew across a road, and a utility shed blew over, trapping one person who was uninjured.
Portage ASOS reported 12 hours of blizzard conditions. Blizzard conditions were also reported in the east end of Kachemak Bay by a spotter.
Road Weather Information System station in Thompson Pass (Elev 2740 ft) reported gust of 80 mph starting at 2:50pm 1/28.
Report from DOT Maintenance Camp in Thompson Pass indicated variable visibility between 0-100 ft. Worst conditions between miles 25-28 on the Richardson Highway.
King Cove AWOS reported a peak gust of 67 knots at 5:23 p.m. on January 26th.

King Salmon Weather Service Office observed 10 inches of new snow.

The snow stake at mile post 69.9 recorded 24 of snow in 24 hours. A school bus went off the road in Moose Pass.

Hatcher Pass Avalanche Center reported an avalanche in Hatcher Pass closed the road to the ski area at the top. 10 people were stranded at the ski area for 24 hours while DOT cleared the road. No one was injured.

A Public weather station on Spendlove Drive recorded a gust to 103 mph. This was the highest gust during the event. Regular gusts up to 70 mph were observed in midtown, with gusts between 80 and 90 mph along the Anchorage Hillside. Up to 27,500 customers were without power at one time during the event. A home along the Anchorage Hillside lost its roof early in the day.

Workers with the Alaska Railroad Corporation discovered a 5 mile section of track flooded and covered with chunks of ice after an ice jam caused a 8-10 ft vertical water level rise between Talkeetna and Curry, on the Susitna River.  Significant sections of track were damaged and moved horizontally by as much as 25 ft. At the same time, significant areas of erosion/damage to the railroad bed itself also occurred which had to be rebuilt. Rail service was disrupted for several days.

As the spring river ice breakup front moved downstream on the Kuskokwim River, an ice jam formed downstream of the villages of Upper Kalskag and Lower Kalskag. The road connecting the two villages was flooded and impassable. Access to the shared power plant was also cut off. Many yards had floodwaters affecting them.

As the spring river ice breakup front moved downstream on the Kuskokwim River, an ice jam formed downstream of the village of Tuluksak. Reports were received of water levels rising rapidly into the lower portions of the village, and the community prepared for more substantial evacuations. Thankfully, the water levels began to slowly fall as the ice jam released slowly.

As the spring river ice breakup front moved downstream on the Kuskokwim River, an ice jam formed near Birch Crossing, downstream of Aniak. Water levels rose steadily in Aniak and began to flood the low-lying areas of town with up to 6 ft depths of water. The most significantly impacted areas were the gravel pit outside of town, and the barge landing downstream of the main town. Eventually the ice jam released and water levels steadily dropped.

The dike eroded along Sawmill Creek causing flooding on 2 properties in the Clyde King Subdivision to flood; 1 house has 1.5 ft of water.

The Yentna and Skwentna rivers, already high due to snowmelt, were expected to reach near bankfull during the second week of July as the weather pattern turned wetter. On July 10th, a local lodge near the confluence of the Yentna River and Lake Creek reported flooding in cabins and outbuildings resulting in 18 inches of water getting inside. The Flood Advisory was issued as a result of this report. Later that same day, an update from Lake Creek was received saying that the river had risen to 2-3 feet above the bank and that most of the property, including numerous water front lodges, were flooded.
The river gauge on the Yentna River at Lake Creek went into minor flood stage for a brief period on August 14th. McDougall's Lodge Cabins were evacuated due to flooding water.

The Resurrection River reached moderate flood stage on Oct 13th and again on the 16th.  Numerous creeks in the Seward area went overbank; closing and washing out roads to critical infrastructure.  The airport runway flooded, and there were mud and rock slides throughout the area.
Adak NWLON reported 5 hours of warning-level wind gusts.
Alaska DOT reported blizzard conditions through Thompson Pass, with blowing snow reducing visibility to less than 1/4 mile.

Due easterly winds and an unusually high tide combined to bring waves of an estimated 8 to 9 feet directly into Whittier's harbor. This caused an extensive amount of damage, which was reported by the harbormaster and public works director. Winds during this time reached between 60 and 75 mph.

The NWLON recorded gusts over 60 mph after 10:32am. The 92 mph was the instantaneous peak gust. General gust speads were in the 50-77 range with winds starting to decrease to less gusty after 10pm. Spotter reports indicated uprooted trees.

Cape Newenham ASOS reported an hour of visibility reduced below 1/4 mile in snow, and 12 hours of winds greater than 35 mph. Peak winds observed were gusts to 71 mph.
Sand Point ASOS measured wind gusts above 70 mph for 4 hours.

Several mesonet stations recorded winds gusts above 73 mph between noon and 4 p.m. The highest gust recorded was 81 mph off Potter Valley Rd.

Palmer ASOS reported 0.44 of precipitation between 5:32 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. This caused localized flooding of parking lots in the Palmer area. Quarter inch hail was also reported at this time.

Late on December 21, an ice jam on Willow Creek near the Deneki Bridge (61.77N, -149.956W) caused water to back up and flow through numerous residences.  Deneki Road and access to the Deneki Bridge was closed for multiple weeks between December 21 and January 8, 2020.  At least thirteen households evacuated on December 21-22 due to flooding or anticipation of road closures.  Six homes were damaged by flood water; there was a report of knee-deep water in one home, as well as deep flowing water around the house, ���It formed a river in my yard��� .  Numerous, (>10), cars were flooded and frozen in place.  Also some cars had to be abandoned after owners tried to drive across the flood waters and became stuck.      ||Examining the hydrographs, the most likely cause of the ice jam flooding was an ice dam which collapsed in the canyon, causing a mini breakup which was constricted and stopped at the Deneki Bridge.  ||The MatSu Borough worked with private contractors to divert the water and allow access to the Deneki Bridge and the subdivision of homes and farms to which it provides the single point of access.  Using heavy equipment, they mechanically removed the ice jam, which allowed the water flow to return to the channel, preventing it from flowing through the neighborhoods overland.

An ice jam formed on the lower Anchor River on April 19, 2021.  Originally the ice jam formed above the stream gage on the Old Sterling Highway and over the next few days the ice jam slowly moved downstream until it broke on April 24th.  The area around the Old Sterling Highway flooded - notably the DOT supply and equipment staging site for the bridge replacement this summer as well as the campgrounds along the Anchor River Road and Anchor River Road itself.

This ice jam was caused by some of the thickest ice on the river this winter - some local reports indicated that it was greater than 50 thick (most other reading along the Kuskokwim from last year are around 36).  Ice became thicker in this region because of freeze up ice jams, where many layers of frazil ice accumulated.  When the breakup front moved to below Aniak, this thick ice jammed.  It held for 5 days and slowly backed up water to Aniak, and Aniak was on the verge of flooding from the back sloughs.  There was water across the road circling the lower end of the runway, as well as flooding the gravel pit and barge landing area.
